output.brief: Resignations are concentrated in one place: 8 of the 11 associates who worked on Kestrel have left, against 1 of 13 who never worked on it. The other groups' attrition is normal, and the firm-wide hours target applies everywhere, so neither general market mobility nor the target explains this group. What we cannot yet tell is whether the cause is the workload on Kestrel or how Dorian Faulk supervises. He is the only partner on Kestrel, so the two overlap completely in the records. Pay is also unresolved. The survey shows some pay concern, but it is only a mid-ranked complaint, and the leavers' own farewell emails give no reasons. I would not announce the retention payment and close the review. It targets the least-supported explanation, and it would be paid to the whole group rather than the Kestrel associates. Next step: run the roughly £9k confidential interviews with leavers and current Kestrel associates. Structure them to separate supervision from workload, and have them run by someone outside the group. Start tracking matter and supervising partner in attrition reporting now. Hold the supervision change and the contract reviewers until the interviews report, which should take about three weeks. Confidence is moderate.
